cues.text: So, Tim, we have to do a short summary of our work experience on a farm.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Right. My farm was great, but arranging the work experience was hard.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: One problem was it was miles away and I don't drive.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: And also, I'd really wanted a placement for a month, but I could only get one for two weeks.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I was lucky, the farmer let me stay on the farm so I didn't have to travel.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: But finding the right sort of farm to apply to wasn't easy.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: No, they don't seem to have websites, do they.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I found mine through a friend of my mother's, but it wasn't easy.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: No.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: My farm was mostly livestock, especially sheep.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I really enjoyed helping out with them.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I was up most of one night helping a sheep deliver a lamb...
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: On your own?
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: No, the farmer was there, and he told me what to do.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: It wasn't a straightforward birth, but I managed.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: It was a great feeling to see the lamb stagger to its feet and start feeding almost straightaway, and to know that it was OK.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Mm.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Then another time a lamb had broken its leg, and they got the vet in to set it, and he talked me through what he was doing.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: That was really useful.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Yes, my farm had sheep too.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: The farm was in a valley and they had a lowland breed called Suffolks, although the farmer said they'd had other breeds in the past.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: So were they bred for their meat?
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Mostly, yes. They're quite big and solid.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: My farm was up in the hills and they had a different breed of sheep, they were Cheviots.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Oh, I heard their wool's really sought after.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Yes. It's very hardwearing and they use it for carpets.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: I was interested in the amount of supplements they add to animals' feed nowadays.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Like, even the chickens got extra vitamins and electrolytes in their feed.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Yes, I found that too. And they're not cheap.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: But my farmer said some are overpriced for what they are.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: And he didn't give them as a matter of routine, just at times when the chickens seemed to particularly require them.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Yes, mine said the same.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: He said certain breeds of chickens might need more supplements than the others, but the cheap and expensive ones are all basically the same.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Mm.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: So did your farm have any other livestock, Diana?
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Yes, dairy cows. I made a really embarrassing mistake when I was working in the milk shed.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Some cows had been treated with antibiotics, so their milk wasn't suitable for human consumption, and it had to be put in a separate container.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: But I got mixed up, and I poured some milk from the wrong cow in with the milk for humans, so the whole lot had to be thrown away.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: The farmer wasn't too happy with me.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: I asked my farmer how much he depended on the vet to deal with health problems.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I'd read reports that the livestock's health is being affected as farmers are under pressure to increase production.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Well, he didn't agree with that, but he said that actually some of the stuff the vets do, like minor operations, he'd be quite capable of doing himself.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Yeah. My farmer said the same.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: But he reckons vets' skills are still needed.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Now we've got to give a bit of feedback about last term's modules - just short comments, apparently.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Shall we do that now?
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: OK. So medical terminology.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Well, my heart sank when I saw that, especially right at the beginning of the course.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: And I did struggle with it.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: I'd thought it'd be hard, but actually I found it all quite straightforward.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: What did you think about diet and nutrition?
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: OK, I suppose.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Do you remember what they told us about pet food and the fact that there's such limited checking into whether or not it's contaminated?
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I mean in comparison with the checks on food for humans - I thought that was terrible.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Mm. I think the module that really impressed me was the animal disease one, when we looked at domesticated animals in different parts of the world, like camels and water buffalo and alpaca.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: The economies of so many countries depend on these, but scientists don't know much about the diseases that affect them.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Yes, I thought they'd know a lot about ways of controlling and eradicating those diseases, but that's not the case at all.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I loved the wildlife medication unit.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Things like helping birds that have been caught in oil spills.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: That's something I hadn't thought about before.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Yeah, I thought I might write my dissertation on something connected with that.
cues.speaker: DIANA

cues.text: Right. So …
cues.speaker: TIM
